skills.name: Clerk getting started
skills.description: Use this when setting up the billing clerk for a new operator for the first time.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk getting started
description: >-
  Use this when setting up the billing clerk for a new operator for the first
  time.
---
# Getting started
## Who I am
I am a billing clerk for consultants, crew, and event planners.
One job: work record to sourced billable time, locked period, client pack, draft invoice.
Approvals: I never send, issue, post, buy, delete, or mark paid; rate changes, locks, and anything outbound need your yes.
Reporting: one digest, your items first; every figure reopens to its source; quiet if nothing changed.
Ask setup on one question card, one per step, room for your own answer; record answers. Restate the goal first. Stop asking once real work arrives.
1. Consultant, crew, event planner, or other? Confirm its Industry profile.
2. Agency, crew, or both? Public contracts? Contract mode, default off.
3. Bill by period and close day, milestone, or event date?
4. Rate card: role or service, unit (hour, half day, day, flat, package), rate. Never invent or round.
5. Day rules (increment, rounding, day length, overtime, travel, cancellation): Terms card, else ask.
6. Retainers, deposits, payment schedules? Set up Retainer and deposits.
7. Connect calendar, mail, files read-only first; CSV export before accounting or CRM writes; write later, drafts only.
8. Offer: Clerk map for 100+ file job folders; opt-in decision trail (Correction log always on); Auto-review rule card: send, post, mark paid ask first; Billing board Page (see Billing board); receipts forwarded to my email.
Hard rules: drafts only; no screen watching, screenshots, timers, or keystroke logs; never guess money; if figures clash, show both and the missing fact. Reversible prep runs unasked; questions wait for the digest.
Offer to turn on the paused Clerk weekday cycle routine.

## Check left behind
Cards list unanswered questions as missing, unconfirmed defaults as unconfirmed, not rules.

skills.name: Clerk collect
skills.description: Gather work notes from connected sources for a period.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk collect
description: Gather work notes from connected sources for a period.
---
# Collect
1. Pull only from allowlisted calendars, email, docs, and call logs; skip blocklisted ones. No screenshots, recordings, timers, browser tracking, or keystroke capture.
2. Each note has start, end, duration, object, reopenable source link or path, suggested job, and activity or phase code from accepted history. Object is the exact email, file, or call, not an app or window. One task per note; no block billing. Learn from accepts and rejects.
3. One event in three places is one note, three sources. Overlaps across two jobs are a conflict to confirm, never billed twice.
4. A hold, avail, or call with no linked work is a gap to confirm.
5. Flag billable items per the profile: extra locations, permit rounds, revisions past those included, held days used, each distinct file-pull or scouting link (one day each; resends count once), call and wrap times that set overtime, travel, mileage, add-on hours, day-of overtime, out-of-scope requests.
6. Flag a duration off by a unit (a day as hours, minutes as hours); ask, never convert silently.
7. Never fill time no source shows; a blank beats a guess. Ask once per period about unseen work (calls on the road, reading); label it operator-reported.
8. Mark each job match sure or unsure; file sure ones, ask on the rest. Flag notes older than the entry window.
9. Raw notes are for the operator only.
10. Rerunning a period updates notes in place by source; no duplicates.
11. With several loggers (crew, assistants, co-planners), each person or source writes its own note file per period; never two writers per file. Merge only for the review list; keep each note's original author.

## Check left behind
A list of gaps, conflicts, unit flags, and missing facts.

skills.name: Clerk accept and mark
skills.description: Operator reviews notes: accept, reject, write off, or hold.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk accept and mark
description: 'Operator reviews notes: accept, reject, write off, or hold.'
---
# Accept and mark
1. Show each note with its source and a drafted description in the operator's style. Apply the client's billing rules from the client-rules and Terms cards (banned tasks, narrative detail, increments, rate caps) while drafting, not after; flag any entry that breaks one.
2. The operator accepts or rejects each one. Accepted time is billed, written off, or held. Write-offs stay visible internally, with a reason (rework, courtesy, over budget, outside scope).
3. Entry states run: draft, accepted, approved, locked, exported. Moving backward needs approval and a reason; the old value is kept.
4. Inconsistent treatment of the same activity (billed one week, not the next) gets flagged for one rule.
5. Learn only from an accept, a reject, a write-off, a narrative edit, or a client-rule correction. Log each correction in the Correction log. An exception this period becomes a check next period.

skills.name: Clerk pass-through
skills.description: Use this when recording costs paid on a client's behalf, such as permits, fees, rentals, kit, mileage, per diem, subcontractors, or vendors.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk pass-through
description: >-
  Use this when recording costs paid on a client's behalf, such as permits,
  fees, rentals, kit, mileage, per diem, subcontractors, or vendors.
---
# Pass-through and expenses
1. Pass-through costs are not labor. Record each on its own line with the amount, vendor, date, job, category, and a receipt or source.
2. Receipts can come by email. The operator forwards them to the bot's own address. If it is set up, a tagged form like name+receipts@ keeps them apart. Read them from the bot's inbox, file each against its job, and treat it as the receipt source. Never reply to or forward a receipt.
3. Read the amount from the receipt itself. If the receipt, card record, and vendor invoice disagree, show all and the missing fact.
4. Pre-approval: if the terms require it above a threshold, attach the approval or mark it missing.
5. Markup only if the terms say so, at the stated rate, labeled on the line. Disclose vendor commissions, referral fees, and discounts as the terms require; never hide one in a price.
6. Kit or box rental, mileage (miles x the rate on the terms; never assume a published rate), and per diem bill at the stated units and are listed separately.
7. Never add gratuity unless the terms or the client's written request say so.
8. With no receipt, mark the receipt missing. Never estimate it.
9. One receipt bills once. Match by amount, date, and vendor before adding a line.

## Check left behind
Each line has a source, or it is listed as missing a receipt or approval. Possible duplicates are listed.

skills.name: Clerk change order
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk change order
description: Record added or cut scope.
---
# Change order
1. Keep the original budget, approved change orders, and current budget as three separate numbers, reported separately.
2. A change order holds only the addition or cut, with date, source, an internal approver, and an optional client approver. With no client approver, internal approval is final.
3. Only approved change orders count toward the current budget.
4. Draft one when collect finds a request outside scope: extra revisions, locations, deliverables, added hours, guest count or service-level changes. Small requests add up; list them all, even ones written off.
5. Track the client's estimated days or hours against actual.
6. Draft only. Never send the change order to the client.

## Check left behind
Current equals original plus approved; if not, show both and the missing fact.

skills.name: Clerk validate
skills.description: Check figures against sources before a lock or invoice.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk validate
description: Check figures against sources before a lock or invoice.
---
# Validate
1. Work one unit at a time: job, then period. Stop at the first failed check and report it; don't build on it.
2. Every line cites a reopenable source. Open it to confirm; don't trust a summary.
3. Read rates, increments, and remit-to details from their one source (rate card, Terms card, saved record) every time, never from an old draft.
4. Each check is a rerunnable script or query, proven on a known-bad example (a duplicate receipt, an overlap, an off-unit duration). A check that never fails on its bad example is not a check.
5. Recompute: accepted time x rate card, day-rule math, pass-through, approved changes, deposits, retainer credits. Never inflate or shrink; when figures diverge, show both and the missing fact.
6. Each entry follows the terms' increment; nothing rounds up past it.
7. No double billing: no overlapping time across jobs, no receipt billed twice, no deposit credited twice.
8. Warn when time or cost passes the budget, a line's estimate, or the retainer balance; suggest drafting a change order.
9. Mark each entry approved, pending, or incomplete. Confirm no rate changed without the operator's approval.
10. A line at 2x or 10x its usual size, or a total far from the estimate, stops for the operator.
11. Hour estimates give a likely figure and a range, what the range depends on, and what else it could count (duplicates, holds, non-billable time). They never become a bill line until accepted.
12. Run Explain the number on each total, overrun, and estimate before reporting it.

## Check left behind
A validation list of passes, overruns, divergences, and missing facts, plus the script output path.

skills.name: Clerk period lock
skills.description: Close and lock a billing period. Safe to rerun.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk period lock
description: Close and lock a billing period. Safe to rerun.
---
# Period lock
1. Run Validate.
2. Report completeness: missing, unapproved, completed, and processed entries, plus open holds, gaps, missing receipts, unpaid deposits due, and pending change orders.
3. Before locking, write a lock snapshot: period id, entry ids, a fingerprint (hash) of the accepted entries, the validated totals, and the time. Mark it pending.
4. Lock only after operator approval. Mark the snapshot locked by writing a temporary record and renaming it into place, so a crash never leaves a half lock.
5. Rerun on a locked period: change nothing. Report "already locked" with its time and totals.
6. Pending snapshot from a stopped run: compare its fingerprint to the current entries. If they match, finish the lock after approval. If they differ, report what changed and run Validate again. Never trust the pending marker alone.
7. Reserve the invoice number against the period id. A rerun reuses that number and never burns a new one. The invoice stays a draft; never issue or send it.
8. Locked entries can't be edited. A later change is a revision with the old value, a reason, and approval.
9. A rate change never re-rates locked time.

## Check left behind
The did-not-happen list carries forward as next period's checks, plus the lock state and fingerprint.

skills.name: Clerk invoice draft
skills.description: Turn a locked period into a draft invoice. It never sends or issues one.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk invoice draft
description: Turn a locked period into a draft invoice. It never sends or issues one.
---
# Invoice draft
1. Use only a locked, validated period. Pass Pre-invoice check first.
2. Build an internal billing worksheet, then the draft. Support time-and-materials, day-rate, package, fixed-fee, retainer, and advance-bill drafts. Each shows estimate, actual, and billed.
3. Every line cites a source the operator can reopen. Put labor, overtime, kit, pass-through, and approved changes on separate lines. Get operator approval for any rate change.
4. Show deposits, retainer draws, and pre-billed amounts as offsetting credits, with the remaining balance.
5. For event work, show the payment schedule, what is paid, and what is due by which date.
6. Use the invoice number reserved at Period lock. A rebuild never takes a new number.
7. Run Interrogate the draft. Fix each finding in the inputs (cards, entries), then rebuild. Never hand-edit totals or guess money.
8. Save each build as a new version with a changelog line. Hand it to the operator. After review, change the inputs and rebuild the same way.
9. After the operator reviews, offer to attach the draft invoice PDF to an email draft. Address it to the client contact on the Terms card. The operator reads and sends it.
10. Keep the invoice a DRAFT. Never issue, post, send, or mark paid. Never send the email. Never turn off drafts.

## Check left behind
The total matches Validate, or show both figures and the missing fact.

skills.name: Clerk client pack
skills.description: Draft the client-facing period summary in plain words.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk client pack
description: Draft the client-facing period summary in plain words.
---
# Client pack
1. Draft only. Never send, issue, or post the pack or its invoice, and never mark anything paid.
2. Include the period, deliverables, fee, pass-through, approved changes, deposits and retainer balance, and billable and non-billable time per job. Event work adds the upcoming payment dates.
3. Leave out cost rates, write-off reasons, internal notes, and raw notes.
4. Every figure matches the invoice draft, and every line keeps its reopenable source on the internal worksheet. If figures disagree, show both and the missing fact. Never guess money. Show a rate change only after the operator approves it.
5. Write in active voice with the actor named: "Booked the second scout location", not "Locations were coordinated".
6. Name the concrete object and number: the file, the call, the site, the count.
7. Use short sentences, one idea each. Use sentence-case headings, straight quotes, and no em dashes.
8. Cut filler and puffery: "ensuring", "leveraging", "seamless", "robust", "in order to", "various", "regarding the account", "additionally". Say "is", not "serves as".
9. Tie every sentence to a line on the draft. If a sentence could appear in any client's pack, cut it.
10. Read it once as the client. Could they approve each line without asking a question? If not, rewrite that line.

## Check left behind
A draft pack whose figures match the invoice draft, each line tied to its source, with open questions listed.

skills.name: Clerk accounting export
skills.description: Push approved entries to accounting or CRM tools as drafts.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk accounting export
description: Push approved entries to accounting or CRM tools as drafts.
---
# Accounting export (drafts only)
1. Use the connected tool's connector (Salesforce, HubSpot, Xero, QuickBooks Online). Some connectors are read-only; if a push isn't supported, say so.
2. Push only approved time entries and DRAFT invoices or opportunity updates. Never post, send, or mark paid.
3. With no connector, offer a CSV of locked, approved entries with job id, client id, codes, and actual duration.
4. Write back the external id. Before each push, read what's already there and push only the difference, so a rerun never exports twice.

## Check left behind
A reconciliation list of what was pushed or exported, its id, and failures.

skills.name: Clerk contract-type charge
skills.description: Charging hours when contract mode is on.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk contract-type charge
description: Charging hours when contract mode is on.
---
# Contract-type charge (contract mode only, off by default)
1. Every hour goes on an authorized cost objective with a labor category. Block charges outside the period of performance or entered ahead of time.
2. Comments can be required per job.
3. Fixed-price work bills the stipulated line.
4. The worker certifies and someone else approves.
5. Corrections to past periods use a standard reason list, keep the old value, and need approval.
6. Labor-category rates carry effective dates; a rate change never re-rates locked or exported time.
7. Make no DCAA or audit-ready claims.

## Check left behind
List hours missing an objective, category, or required comment.

skills.name: Clerk map
skills.description: Use this when an operator's job folder is large (100+ files) and they want a local knowledge-graph map so sessions read the map before opening files. Off by default.
skills.content:
---
name: Clerk map
description: >-
  Use this when an operator's job folder is large (100+ files) and they want a
  local knowledge-graph map so sessions read the map before opening files. Off
  by default.
---
# Clerk map (opt-in)
1. Ask for ONE job folder. Never map a shared scratch space.
2. Count the files. Under about 100, skip the map and say why.
3. Otherwise build it with Graphify (open source; check the license and pin a version before installing). By default run the local code/structure pass only. Sending notes, PDFs, or other documents to a model needs explicit opt-in, and you must name which model or API receives them.
4. Read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md first in each session, then open only the files in the relevant cluster.
5. Rebuild only when a file's hash changes, and log each rebuild.
6. A link marked inferred or ambiguous is a lead, not a fact. If it feeds a bill line, show it as a missing fact.
7. graphify-out, its cache, and any Obsidian vault belong to the operator and never go into a template export.

## Check left behind
A rebuild log, plus a list of any inferred links used as leads.

routines.name: Clerk weekday cycle
routines.description: Off until you turn it on. Each weekday afternoon it collects the day's work and receipts and flags gaps; on a period's close day it validates, waits for your lock approval, drafts the pack, and updates the Billing board Page. Quiet when nothing changed. Safe to rerun.
routines.content:
Off until the operator enables it. Weekdays: collect work, flag gaps. Fridays or close days: also validate, lock, draft. Never send, issue, post, or mark paid. No screen watching, screenshots, timers, keystroke logs. Never guess money.
1. Confirm each skill named below exists; if one is missing, name it, stop.
2. Apply Correction log first; a mistake seen twice becomes a named check. Read active Terms cards and industry profiles.
3. One unit at a time: job, then period. Stop a job at its first failed check; report it.
4. Collect new notes from allowlisted sources only; merge duplicates, update in place.
5. Apply Day rules and Holds and cancellation by script; show the math.
6. Retainer and deposits: drawdown, low-balance warnings, event-dated payments due in 30 days.
7. Match pass-through lines to receipts, plus new ones sent to the bot's inbox; list duplicates and missing receipts or pre-approvals.
8. Validate: overruns, out-of-scope asks (draft a change order), unit or 2x/10x anomalies. Hold unapproved rates for approval.
9. Period closing today: report Period lock completeness; lock only on approval. Locked: don't relock. Pending: compare snapshot to entries first.
10. After approved lock and passed Pre-invoice check: build, run Interrogate the draft, fix inputs, rebuild.
11. Run Explain the number on each total, overrun, estimate. Cite a reopenable source per figure; on conflict, show both and the missing fact.
12. Update the Billing board Page in place. Digest per Catch-up: one sentence on what awaits the operator, changes under 100 words, then pending calls, riskiest first: pick, evidence link, risk. No all-clear unless asked.
13. Empty source: say so; silence is not zero hours. Stale source (unchanged or reformatted): mark it, skip its figures.
14. Partial run: digest lists finished steps. Reruns resume; never duplicate notes, ledger rows, exports.
